one_month_reasoning: In the window to 2026-11-19: Q3 2026 results (date still unannounced; the company announces ~2 weeks ahead; ~2026-11-04/05 after close by analogy with 2025-11-05) and the end of the 60-day lock-up from the 2026-09-09 424B5 on ~2026-11-08. Q3 is usually Centrus's smallest delivery quarter (FY revenue guide $450-500M vs H1 $252.8M puts most of H2 in Q4) and costs and stock comp are rising, so a weak Q3 print is expected; the guide reaffirmation, the first Westerman contribution and any phase-1 capex figure matter more. The lock-up binds the company and insiders, not the offering's buyers, so its supply effect is small; it does reopen the ATM/follow-on window. Possible news on the pending 2026-27 Russian import waiver, TENEX export licences and post-2026-09-30 HALEU cascade arrangements. No Investor Day is scheduled (round 1's December date could not be confirmed). The stock is down 37% since early September with ~30% of float short, so a reversal and further momentum are both live. No strong signal: a near-symmetric lognormal centred at ~$108 with monthly vol 0.25 (89%/3.5), slightly below spot for sector momentum and the reopened issuance window; P(>= $109.88) = 0.472.

At ~$195/SWU realised, ~$1,235 per SWU/yr of capex and Urenco-like 45-47% margins, the LEU build is NPV-negative (-197.1) and value rests on the DOE-funded HALEU task order (+616.7), Westerman at cost and $567M net cash at the horizon over 25.24M shares. bear.story: The first phase-1 cost disclosure shows ~$2.5B+ and LEU contract prices that do not clear a 10% return; HALEU demand slips with advanced-reactor licensing; the 2026-27 waiver or TENEX licences break; a below-value equity raise funds the gap; nuclear sentiment keeps de-rating. Price heads toward net cash plus the DOE-backed HALEU milestones (~$30-40).

base.story: Piketon stays on its 2029 schedule; the DOE milestones and X-energy/Antares/Radiant offtakes hold; 2027 trading margins hold under the waivers; Westerman adds ~$130M of third-party revenue. The market keeps part of its strategic premium but marks the LEU build toward Urenco-like economics (term SWU ~$180-200), so the price drifts between my $47 fair value and today's level.

bull.story: Term SWU moves to $240+ as the Russian ban bites before Western additions (Urenco 2032-36, Orano IKE 2032-39, GLE from 2030); the first cost disclosure shows capex near Orano-like ~$740/SWU-yr (variant fair value $56 rising with price) and a path to ~3.5M SWU; HALEU contracts firm up with prepayments; shorts (~30% of float) cover.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The core is a finite resale stream (FY2025 LEU gross profit $111.5M on $346.2M) that ends with the Russian supply cliff (TENEX 2028, Orano 2030), with a 3.6% TTM EBITDA margin, against BWXT's/CEG's/VST's owned long-lived assets, so a deep discount persists by construction. Because NTM core EBITDA at the horizon is ~$4M, the multiple adds no information beyond net cash and gets no weight; the plant is valued in rNPV and the 2034 exit multiples (11x / 13x) sit below the 14.0x median for single-site, liability-heavy enrichment.

thesis_break_reason: $40 is about the horizon cash floor ($19.83/share: net cash after the build-out spend and an expected raise, run-off, Westerman at cost, less corporate cost incl. SBC) plus the DOE task-order milestones (~$24.4/share) net of the at-risk HALEU operating leg. Trading there would mean the market doubts even the government-backed HALEU build or the cash: a DOE funding cut, a Piketon halt or a dilutive rescue raise, i.e. something fundamental, not volatility. On the upside, sustained trading above ~$190 with a disclosed capex/SWU below ~$800 and term SWU above $250 would break my bearish thesis.

reasoning: Industry lane, revised after the supervisor's review. The rest of the chain says enrichment is tight but new capacity is expensive: Urenco's order book rose to EUR27.3B and spot SWU sits at $200 (Urenco H1-26), term ~$180 (Silex, Aug-26), yet US utilities paid only $108.70/SWU on average in 2025 (EIA) because contracts lag, and Urenco earns ~38-47% EBITDA margins (FY2025; S&P 2027 forecast). New centrifuge capacity costs ~$676-740/SWU-yr at Orano's scale (IKE; GB2 extension) and ~$1,400 on the inflation-adjusted ACP history; a 16M+ SWU Western wave (Orano IKE, GLE, Urenco) lands as Centrus ramps. Centrus today is a trader: 'well over one-half' of 2027 deliveries are TENEX-sourced and US waivers end 2027-12-31, so FY2028 is a gap year before Piketon's 2029 first output and the engine runs no DCF. Round-2 changes: Westerman is bigger than I had (424B5: ~$160M 2025 revenue, bought at 0.73x sales vs Worthington's ~1.0x in 2012), now valued at cost $116M and ~$130M of third-party revenue in the core years; SBC is counted once (no share growth; a fuller ~$30M/yr corporate line incl. SBC, -$297M PV); an expected raise (p0.5 x $350M at $95) enters shares (25.24M) and net cash ($567M at H); the DOE milestones are their own part at 6.5% (supervisor 5.5%) with declining probabilities; the 3.0x EV/sales leg (round-1 $69.87) is replaced by a 6.0x EV/EBITDA check at weight 0; the unconfirmed December Investor Day is out of the catalysts. Build: LEU -197.1, HALEU ops -55.5, DOE milestones +616.7, expansion +26.8, run-off, Westerman, TS, corporate cost, net cash: SOTP $35.31; market-share states $72.66 and cash floor + option $44.0 bracket it; fair value $46.82 (round 1 $47.44). Orano-like capex variant $55.94 (+20%), the swing factor I flag for Kilian; I keep ~$1,235/SWU-yr (supervisor ~$1,350) and do not bank the ~$300M Palantir savings claim. Reverse DCF: today's price needs ~2.6x my base EBITDA, between my base and bull states. For the ladder I still do not assume convergence to my value within 12 months: prices beat fundamentals as 12-month forecasts, the first capex disclosure can surprise either way, nuclear names carry a sentiment premium and short interest is ~30%. Median ~$79 (about 55% weight on spot in log terms; nudged from $80 for the reopened issuance window), lognormal sigma 0.75, giving P(>= $110) = 0.329.

Base p0.50: LEU 1.2M SWU (9% of US demand) x $195 = $234M at 47% EBITDA (S&P's 2027 Urenco forecast midpoint EUR950M / EUR2,000M) = $110M; HALEU 12 MTU (24% of DOE's 50 MT) x 41 SWU/kg x $350 = $172M at 55% = $95M; Westerman (~$140M third-party) + TS (~$30M) at 10% = $17M; corporate cost incl. SBC not in plant margins -$30M; EBITDA $192M x 11x = $2.11B; 2034 net cash $663M (H $567M + DOE milestones $681M probability-weighted - remaining capex $1.13B + operating cash ~$450M + run-off $95M); equity $2775M / 24.87M sh (25.24M - 0.47M 2030-note shares in today's count + 0.10M at a ~$100 2030 price) = $111.6 (2034) / 1.97 = $56.6. Bull p0.30: LEU 2.6M SWU (20% of US demand) x $240 at 55% = $343M; HALEU 24 MTU (48% of DOE 50 MT) x 41 x $400 at 60% = $236M; +17 -30 = $566M EBITDA x 13x = $7.36B; net cash $2268M (base - $1.8B more capex + $0.6B extra operating cash + ~$2.0B common-warrant exercise (424B5: four series of ~$500M each), 6.99M sh at $227-363, + $805M 2032 notes converted instead of repaid); equity $9626M / 37.38M sh (+6.99M warrants, +3.51M 2032-note shares at $229.62, 2030 notes net-share settled at ~$200: +2.12M) = $257.5 / 1.97 = $130.72. Value = 0.2 x 25.7 + 0.5 x 56.6 + 0.3 x 130.72 = $72.66.

Option: underlying S = unrisked PV at H of Piketon LEU ($505M) + HALEU operating cash ($435M) + DOE task-order milestones ($706M PV at 10%) = $1.65B (round-1 rNPV parts; unchanged); strike K = PV at 10% of remaining phase-1 capex $1.13B = $0.98B; sigma 45% (term SWU went from ~$60 in 2020 to ~$180 in 2026; below the 89% equity vol because the equity is levered to the project); T = 2 yrs (go/no-go on LEU cascades before 2029 first output); r = 4.0%. model_inputs.structure_note: Value is carried by an explicit sum of the parts (weight 0.50): rNPV of the Piketon build per programme (LEU contingent book; HALEU 12 MTU operations; expansion option), the $900M DOE HALEU task-order milestones as their own probability-weighted cash-flow part at a government-payer rate, a cash-flow run-off of the legacy TENEX/Orano trading book, Westerman at cost, Technical Solutions, and a negative corporate-cost part that carries SBC; two custom legs (market-share scenarios 0.25, cash floor + option 0.25). The EV/EBITDA cross-check is shown at weight 0 (the run-off core's NTM EBITDA at H is ~$4M, so it adds no information beyond net cash). The three consolidated years (FY2026-28) describe the existing business only (expansion capex sits in rNPV dev costs after the horizon and in net_debt_horizon before it). FY2028 is the gap year between the end of Russian LEU imports to the US (waivers end 2027-12-31) and first Piketon output (2029), so core NOPAT is negative (-$12.9M) and the engine sets the DCF weight to 0 (pre-profit rule); the plant's cash flows are valued in rNPV rather than by fading a trough year.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) phase-1 capex ~$2.1B (~$1,235 per SWU/yr) is my low-confidence estimate (company: 'multi-billion' only); the supervisor reconciled ~$1,350. VARIANT at Orano-like cost (~$740/SWU-yr: GB2 extension EUR1.7bn / 2.5M SWU; IKE ~$5B / 7.4M SWU = $676): post-horizon phase-1 and expansion capex x 0.60 lifts fair value from $46.70 to $55.94 (+20%; computed before the citation-gate warrant-cash correction, which lifts the base to $46.82); this moves value >5%, so flagged. (2) HALEU priced on SWU (customer-supplied feed) at $350/SWU vs $415/SWU implied by DOE's $17.0M/MTU option price. (3) DCF weight 0 because the FY2028 core is a trough by construction (Russian import ban, no Piketon output yet): the supervisor's core has FY2028 EBIT ~+$7M; mine is -$15M because I carry ~$85M of corporate, advanced-technology and SBC cost against a ~$58M LEU gross profit. If the core were positive, the engine's DCF on the run-off core would need the build-out in `rnpv` adjustment mode. (4) DOE milestones discounted at 6.5% (supervisor 5.5%): DOE credit is sovereign but the FY2027 request does not fund cascade operation and payment timing depends on appropriations, so I add ~1pt over the 10-year; performance risk sits in declining probabilities 0.85/0.82/0.80/0.75. (5) No `contracts` entry: the $900M task order pays against capacity deployment milestones, so it is a probability-weighted part, not a signed fixed schedule. (6) fair_value.value equals the engine base horizon value.
